settings.tagline: Rooted in Ruiru Since 2025 · Neighbours Walking Together in Practical Care & Hope.
settings.heroHeadline: A Community Circle Where Every Neighbour Is Seen and Held.
settings.heroSubheadline: Started in Ruiru, Kiambu County in 2025, His & Hers Circle of Hope is a Christian community-based organisation bringing neighbours, families, elders living alone, mental health and trauma care, rehabilitation pathways, and partner children’s homes together long after any single outreach day ends.
settings.welcomeHeadline: Where Neighbours, Families & Partner Homes Carry One Another Through
settings.welcomeBody: In Ruiru, an elder may quietly wonder what to cook for supper while a neighbour a few doors away has spare unga to share. We started His & Hers Circle of Hope so those neighbours meet—connecting households to mental health and trauma support, rehabilitation recovery partners, discreet safe refuge, children’s homes, and ongoing elder fellowship.
settings.prayerInvitation: Whether you come because you could use a hand or because you have one to offer, karibu sana. There is room for you in our circle.
settings.closingStatement: At His & Hers Circle of Hope, no older neighbour sits forgotten, no parent carrying heavy needs is left unheard, and every table leaves room for kindness.

asdGuides.title: Grounding the Body When Old Trauma Feels Present
asdGuides.summary: Unresolved shock and long-term stress live in the body’s alarm system—causing tight chests, jumpiness, or sudden numbness long after a crisis ends.
practicalSteps: Press both feet flat against the floor and notice the solid weight of the chair supporting your back.
Slowly look around the room and name three everyday objects aloud to signal to your brain that today is safe.
Place one warm hand over your breastbone or arm and lengthen your exhale twice as long as your inhale.

asdGuides.title: Interrupting Evening Overwhelm & Spiralling Thoughts
asdGuides.summary: Constant worry over bills, work, or unsafe nights keeps cortisol elevated until sleep refuses to come. Gentle evening boundaries help the mind lay down its load.
practicalSteps: Write tomorrow’s three non-negotiable concerns onto paper 45 minutes before bed so you do not rehearse them in the dark.
Rinse wrists with cool water or sip warm herbal tea away from breaking-news feeds and tense group chats.
Repeat the slow 4-4-6 cadence for five rounds while dropping your shoulders down from your ears.

asdGuides.title: Sitting Beside Carers Before Burnout Takes Over
asdGuides.summary: Mothers, fathers, grandparents, and relatives caring for chronically ill elders or children with high needs rarely get asked: “And how are you doing?”
practicalSteps: Name your exhaustion without guilt—caring faithfully does not mean pretending you have endless energy.
Ask one trusted neighbour or ward prayer partner to hold a 30-minute practical errand or meal drop once a week.
Connect with our Mental Health & Trauma desk or Home Visits circle for an unhurried listening cup of tea.

asdGuides.title: Walking Slowly Through Grief, Betrayal & Honest Prayer
asdGuides.summary: Faith never demands fake smiles when your heart is breaking. Across our circle, grief is met with patience, shared tears, practical soup or unga, and quiet presence.
practicalSteps: Give yourself permission to step away from loud advice that minimizes real heartbreak or loss.
Stay anchored to one honest weekly rhythm—a shared meal, a ward prayer walk, or a confidential call.
Reach out to our Helpline or Administrators & Help Desk so someone walks beside you past outreach day.

impactProjects.title: Children’s Home Mentorship & Care Hamper Day
impactProjects.summary: Corporate volunteers and community friends partnered together to spend a joyful day reading, playing, and equipping a partner children’s home.
impactProjects.whatWasDone: HIS AND HERS coordinated a vetted corporate CSR team and local storytellers to bring reading books, school packs, fresh produce, and unhurried mentorship games to a partner children’s home.
impactProjects.whyItMattered: Children thrive on genuine presence and long-term care, not drop-off charity. Structured visits ensure safeguarding, warmth, and real friendship.
impactProjects.whoItServed: 42 children aged 3–16 alongside house mothers and dedicated residential caregivers.
impactProjects.whatGlowHopedToAchieve: To connect caring organisations and everyday individuals directly with verified children’s homes.
impactProjects.documentedStory: Under wide courtyard trees, teams read stories side by side, shared fruit and lunch, and pledged ongoing termly stationery support.
impactProjects.imageAlt: Corporate volunteers and community members reading with children at a partner children home

impactProjects.title: Youth Encouragement & Mental Wellbeing Circles
impactProjects.summary: Intergenerational mentorship and listening tables creating safe spaces for young people to speak openly, receive guidance, and lighten emotional burdens.
impactProjects.whatWasDone: We hosted welcoming afternoon sessions pairing trained community mentors, counsellors, and educators with youth for open dialogue and emotional wellbeing conversations.
impactProjects.whyItMattered: Many young people carry quiet pressures around mental health, family stress, and belonging. Having trusted adults who listen breaks isolation.
impactProjects.whoItServed: Teenagers, students, and young adults from across diverse neighbourhoods.
impactProjects.whatGlowHopedToAchieve: To cultivate a supportive environment where young people feel heard, safe, and connected to caring mentors and counsellors.
impactProjects.documentedStory: Seated around long wooden tables with notebooks and tea, mentors and students reflected on emotional resilience, hope, and community care.
impactProjects.imageAlt: Community mentors and youth seated together around wooden tables in warm conversation

impactProjects.title: Ruiru Four-Ward Walk, Elder Blankets & Ruiru Boys Student Parcels
impactProjects.locationLabel: Four Wards Across Ruiru, Kiambu County
impactProjects.summary: Convened by Nancy Kariuki and the GLOW Prayer Movement alongside well-wishers—walking four Ruiru wards in prayer while gathering blankets for elders and maize flour, rice, and sugar for student homes at Ruiru Boys.
impactProjects.whatWasDone: Neighbours walked and prayed together across four Ruiru wards, delivering thick warm blankets directly to older residents living alone and sharing bags of maize flour, rice, sugar, lunch, and encouragement at Ruiru Boys student homes.
impactProjects.whyItMattered: Compassion stays alive when outreach becomes steady relationship—ensuring elders know whom to call on cold nights and students hear sincere encouragement over a shared meal.
impactProjects.whoItServed: Older neighbours across four Ruiru wards and boarding student households at Ruiru Boys.
impactProjects.whatGlowHopedToAchieve: To weave prayer and practical neighbourliness into an ongoing circle leading straight into Christmas of Hope.
impactProjects.documentedStory: After walking and praying along dusty morning roads, conveners and friends shared an unhurried meal at Ruiru Boys, exchanging heartfelt words of encouragement.
impactProjects.imageAlt: Warm blankets, maize flour, and sugar carried thoughtfully to a smiling elder neighbour on a stone veranda in Ruiru

impactProjects.title: Safe Refuge & Rehabilitation Pathways Evening
impactProjects.locationLabel: HIS AND HERS Care Family Sanctuary
impactProjects.summary: An open-door evening combining gentle worship, confidential counselling, rehabilitation referrals, and safe-refuge guidance.
impactProjects.whatWasDone: We opened our gathering space for a calm evening featuring acoustic reflection, one-on-one counselling check-ins, and guided referrals to partner rehab and shelter facilities.
impactProjects.whyItMattered: Families battling trauma, addiction, or domestic danger need trustworthy bridges to nearby care facilities without shame.
impactProjects.whoItServed: Individuals, families seeking rehabilitation partners, and survivors rebuilding stability.
impactProjects.whatGlowHopedToAchieve: To bridge spiritual care, mental health listening, and practical safeguarding under one welcoming roof.
impactProjects.documentedStory: As evening settled over the sanctuary, attendees connected with counsellors, rehab liaisons, and prayer companions in warmth and dignity.
impactProjects.imageAlt: Sunlit restoration centre garden where counsellor and family member sit together
